title: Avoiding Sanitary Tees on Horizontal Drain Lines
description: A common error in gravity drainage installation is placing a standard sanitary tee on a horizontal flow line. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for vertical-to-horizontal transitions or vent connections. When installed horizontally, the short sweep fails to direct solid waste properly, leading to frequent blockages and sluggish drainage over time. Code requires a long-sweep elbow, a wye with a 1/8 bend, or a combination fitting for horizontal-to-horizontal changes in direction. Always verify your local plumbing code and fitting orientation to ensure smooth waste transit and proper atmospheric venting.

Avoiding Sanitary Tees on Horizontal Drain Lines

A common error in gravity drainage installation is placing a standard sanitary tee on a horizontal flow line. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for vertical-to-horizontal transitions or vent connections. When installed horizontally, the short sweep fails to direct solid waste properly, leading to frequent blockages and sluggish drainage over time. Code requires a long-sweep elbow, a wye with a 1/8 bend, or a combination fitting for horizontal-to-horizontal changes in direction. Always verify your local plumbing code and fitting orientation to ensure smooth waste transit and proper atmospheric venting.
